chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Khalid ibn Muhammad, from his grandfather Sufyan ibn al-Samti, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who loves that his water and his children be abundant, so let him be habitual in eating the endive.

key_terms.الْهِنْدَبَاءِ: the endive (a type of leafy green vegetable)
key_terms.مَاؤُهُ: his water (referring to bodily fluids, milk, or vitality)

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of eating endive according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the habitual consumption of endive (*al-hindaba'*) to increased bodily fluids (such as milk) and progeny, reflecting the Shia tradition of *al-tibb al-nabawi* where specific foods possess inherent spiritual and physical virtues. This narration underscores the holistic view of health in Shia jurisprudence, where dietary habits are not merely nutritional but also contribute to *barakah* (blessing) and vitality, aligning with the broader Islamic emphasis on maintaining the body as an amanah (trust).
